meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to everyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He hanged himself out of jealousy.
Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'back', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Name me at least one reason.

examples.text: Всем назад, не подходите ко мне!
examples.trans: Everyone back, do not come near me!

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
Yes, it is just so unexpected.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'suit', paired with 'подойти'.

examples.text: Всем назад, не подходите ко мне!
examples.trans: Everyone back, do not come near me!
Do not come near me right now!
Let's go, our turn in the queue is coming up.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
Hello, Viktor Petrovich.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
I am inspecting your restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: Chef, excuse me, please.
Please do not kill me.
Let me go from here, please.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'do', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Why did you do that just now?
I did just that yesterday.
Timur, what have you done here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Is everything alright with you?
We will wash everything out quickly.
We will fix everything!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of total nonsense is this?
Now we will think of something, Chef.
Timur, what have you done here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is asking for', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Я тебя в прошлый раз просил.
examples.trans: I asked you last time.
Please do everything that he asks.
I apologise.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
Hello, Viktor Petrovich.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Who is going to climb in after him now?
And now I have understood everything.
And now pull up your pants quickly.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We will wash everything out quickly.
Quickly hold him right here!
Lyova, fly quickly to the bank.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'тянуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'pull up'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и подтянуть вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and pull up on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют подтянуть.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to pull up.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pants' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And now pull up your pants quickly.
I told you, pull up your pants!
The pants are too long.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
What kind of total nonsense is this?
Chef, those were just coconuts.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You will not withstand a blow from a coconut.
Why did you do that just now?
How foolish you are!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'said', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: You said the wife was on me.
I told you, pull up your pants!
You said to bring him down.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Let us make a bet then.
Let us test it right now!
Enough, let us sort this out calmly.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to punch
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'дарить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'hit, strike!', paired with 'ударять'.

examples.trans: Then why did you hit me?
Lightning just struck me.
Well, come on, hit me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'his', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
Of course, you are completely free.
What kind of report will he write now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: You must not be overfed right now.
Maybe tomorrow, or maybe right now.
Let us test it right now!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We will wash everything out quickly.
We will fix everything!
We do not wish you any harm.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Look, he is still right there!
And there came to be even more money.
And I will save up more for myself.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Enough, let us sort this out calmly.
And we will part ways peacefully.
We can still reach an agreement calmly!

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говориться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to reach an agreement', paired with 'договариваться'.

examples.trans: And we will try to reach an agreement with him.
We can still reach an agreement calmly!
We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Open up, he will freeze in there.
No, he did not come in here.
There are no other people inside there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just do not worry.
You will not withstand a blow from a coconut.
I will not withstand such a blow?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'end' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Of course, you are completely free.
He will definitely crawl to the end.
We are already running out of vases.

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'run', paired with 'побежать'.

examples.trans: I am running to the bank!
That is so she does not run away.
People do that when they want to escape.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
Thank you for the kind words.
What kind of total nonsense is this?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верх').

examples.trans: Senya, run upstairs after him!
Let us run upstairs quickly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you for the kind words.
Denis, thank you, you are my savior!
Thanks, Dad!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, did my husband stop by here?
After all, I live with my mother.
Denis, thank you, you are my savior!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'паситель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'savior' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Denis, thank you, you are my savior!

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть спаситель.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always savior.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: You can live at my place for free!
I live in a communal flat.
I want to live normally.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, Viktor Petrovich.
I am inspecting your restaurant.
Hello, I am very pleased to meet you.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'платно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You can live at my place for free!
If they're late, the pizza is free.
Children get in free.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.trans: Soon they will bring us this money.
I promised that I would quit soon.
Let us run upstairs quickly!
